title: Deep clustering identifies progression subtypes in Huntington's disease
summary: Multisymptom trajectories from Enroll-HD were aligned and clustered with VaDER (variational deep embedding with recurrence), giving two subtypes: stable (n=7122) and rapidly progressive (n=411), which correlated with CAG length and cognitive impairment. A model predicted the subtype from first-visit data, with an independent validation set of pre-manifest patients (n=372). Observational registry data; no causal claim.
ai_technology: VaDER deep clustering of aligned trajectories and a learned subtype-prediction model
organization: Fraunhofer Institute for Algorithms and Scientific Computing

evidence.tested: Independent validation set of pre-manifest patients' manifest-phase data.
evidence.unknown: Prognostic model metrics were not read; clinical utility.
